name: watch-plain
prompt: /video a luxury wristwatch product film, a 9:16 reel for Instagram, 12 seconds, with sound
result:
I made the reel: **`elaris_reel_9x16.mp4`**. It's 1080×1920 (9:16), 30fps, exactly 12.0s, H.264 with AAC stereo sound, about 31 MB. A note first: `/video` isn't a command in this session, so it didn't run. Everything was built with Python (NumPy/Pillow) and ffmpeg.

I checked the frames along the timeline and at each cut, and measured the audio. I haven't watched or listened to it in real time, so give it a play before you post.

**Shots**
| Time | Shot |
|---|---|
| 0 to 2.6s | Fade up on a close-up of the 12 o'clock and the dial's brand name while light sweeps across the blue sunburst dial and a reflection crosses the glass |
| 2.6 to 5.2s | Close-up on the gold hands, caption **EVERY SECOND** |
| 5.2 to 8.0s | The date window and crown, caption **BECOMES AN HEIRLOOM** |
| 8.0 to 12s | Pull back to the full watch on a brown alligator strap. **ÉLARIS** lands at 9.55s and **THE MIDNIGHT COLLECTION** at 10.15s |

Each cut has a short warm-gold flash. The watch reads 10:10, and the seconds hand reaches 12 at 11.0s, timed to the last tick.

**Sound** (all synthesized, so there are no licensing issues)
- A low piano-and-pad bed in D minor that lifts into a brighter chord at the 8s pull-back.
- Ticking every half-second, slightly stronger on each whole second, ending on a final tick at 11.0s.
- A rising whoosh into each cut and a deep boom on it, with a bigger boom on the logo.
- Bell chimes on the logo and tagline, with reverb across the mix.
- Loudness is set for Instagram, around −14 LUFS (measured −13.2) with peaks at −1.5 dB.

**Things to know**
- **"ÉLARIS" is a made-up placeholder brand**, as are "Maison de Haute Horlogerie" and "Midnight · 40 mm". If this is for a real product, tell me the name and copy, or send real photos or a 3D render to use instead of the generated watch.
- The text is placed clear of Instagram's top bar and bottom caption area, and kept centred away from the right-hand buttons.
- Both captions now finish fading before their cuts; in my first encode they bled faintly into the next shot.

**Files** in the project folder:
- `render.py`: the picture
- `audio.py`: the score
- `score.wav`: the raw audio
- `frames/`: the 360 PNG frames

The timing, wording, colours and camera moves are all easy to change and re-render in under a minute.
